simple.meaning: מִזְרָע (mizrâʻ) is a Hebrew action word meaning “a planted field.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 1 time in Isaiah, beginning at Isaiah 19:7. Its meaning becomes clearer as the uses are compared.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to מִזְרָע (H4218) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: מִזְרָע (mizrâʻ) / H4218 is traced through Isaiah 19:7 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.full: H4218. mizra [ מִזְרָע ] noun [masculine] place of sowing, seed-land , only construct יְאוֺר מִזְרַע כֹּל Isa 19:7 (|| יְאוֺר עָרוֺת ); > Du who translates seed (compare מאכל etc.) on accusative of following verb נִדַּף . II. זרע (compare Arabic stretch out, extend , especially arm or leg; power , forearm ).
